title: Academic writing: making sense
subtitle: advocate, infer, empirical, denote, notwithstanding
summary: Present arguments and comment on research the way academic writing does - advocate, deduce, infer, complement - and swap everyday verbs for their academic equivalents.

lesson.heading: Presenting arguments and commenting on others' work
rows: reach a conclusion by thinking carefully about the known facts
Look at these sentences and see if you can deduce how the imperfect tense is used.
From contemporary accounts of his research, we can infer that results were slower to come than he had anticipated.
combine well with another piece of work so each becomes more effective
Elswick's (2016) research complements that of Johnson (2012).
Their research, fortunately, does not overlap.

lesson.heading: Adjectives for describing academic work
rows: based on what is observed rather than on theory
research based on a survey of the population
a poem which can be understood in two quite different ways
an argument which is well-expressed and easy to follow
a textbook which gives a broad overview of an entire discipline
a textbook written by the most highly regarded expert in the field

lesson.heading: Talking about figures
lesson.text: Figures described as **arbitrary** are based on chance or personal choice rather than on a system or supporting data. Figures that **deviate from** the norm are different from what is typical, and statistics that **distort** the picture give a false impression.

examples.text: The sociologists chose their subjects in an **arbitrary** fashion, not a balanced one.
Ulla's mark **deviated** noticeably **from** the average of 68%.
examples.note: = it was much higher or much lower
= present the facts in a misleading fashion

lesson.heading: Talking about processes and frequency
lesson.text: The **incidence** of something such as a disease is how often it occurs. Something **predominant** is the largest in number. Things that happen **in sequence** happen in a particular order, and something **widespread** happens in many places or affects many people.

examples.text: The **incidence** of asthma in children is increasing.
examples.note: = the number of asthmatic children is going up

examples.text: Brown eyes are **predominant** in this population.
The stages of the process occur **in sequence**.
There were **widespread** outbreaks of the illness, and **widespread** alarm.

lesson.heading: Academic verbs and their everyday equivalents
rows: be a sign of, stand for

lesson.heading: Academic expressions and their everyday equivalents

lesson.text: You deduce from the facts in front of you; you infer indirectly, from what is only implied.

exercises.prompt: The French and Swedish teams work in similar areas, but their research, fortunately, does not ___ .
exercises.explanation: If work overlaps with other work, it partially covers the same material.

exercises.prompt: The French data ___ the Swedish data very well - each set makes the other more effective.
exercises.explanation: If one piece of work complements another, they combine well and each becomes more effective.

exercises.prompt: Look at the complete set of graphs and see if you can ___ the rules governing the data from them.
exercises.hint: (work it out from the known facts)
exercises.explanation: To deduce something is to reach a conclusion by thinking carefully about the known facts.

exercises.prompt: This article ___ a different approach to the problem.
exercises.hint: (third person singular: argues in favour of)
exercises.explanation: To advocate something is to argue in favour of it.

exercises.prompt: A great deal can be ___ about the artist's state of mind from his later works.
exercises.explanation: To infer something is to reach a conclusion indirectly.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective with the kind of work it best describes.

pairs.right: a textbook written by the most highly regarded expert in the field
research based on a survey of the population
a poem which can be understood in two quite different ways
an argument which is well-expressed and easy to follow
a textbook which gives a broad overview of an entire discipline

exercises.prompt: If the incidence of asthma in children is increasing, what is going up?
exercises.explanation: The incidence of something is how often it occurs.

exercises.prompt: If facts are distorted, how are they presented?
exercises.explanation: Statistics that distort the picture give a false impression.

exercises.statement: If sociologists choose their research subjects in an arbitrary fashion, they take care to get an appropriate balance of backgrounds.
exercises.explanation: No - arbitrary means based on chance or personal choice rather than on a system, so the selection is random.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: The information ___ in archives that must not be opened until 2050.
exercises.explanation: Reside is the academic equivalent of lie or live.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: He ___ his theory while still a young man.
exercises.explanation: To conceive an idea is the academic way of saying to think it up.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: Each of the symbols in the phonetic alphabet ___ a sound.
exercises.explanation: Denote means be a sign of, or stand for.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: This study contradicted what was previously held to be true, and so ___ a great deal of discussion amongst specialists.
exercises.explanation: Trigger is the academic equivalent of cause.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: Details of the experiment have been ___ to the report.
exercises.explanation: To append something is to add it at the end.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: Jelowski's book ___ the rise and fall of great Empires over two millennia.
exercises.explanation: To reflect upon something is the academic way of saying to think about it.

exercises.prompt: Make it academic: She perceives the Roman Empire as an ___ of a pattern that has repeated itself elsewhere.
exercises.explanation: An instance of something is the academic equivalent of an example of something.

exercises.prompt: Academic rewrite: 'It would appear to show the opposite of what he claimed' becomes ...
options: It would appear to demonstrate the converse of what he claimed.
It would appear to append the converse of what he claimed.
It would appear to negate the instance of what he claimed.
It would appear to reside somewhat of what he claimed.
exercises.explanation: Demonstrate/indicate = show; the converse = the opposite.

exercises.prompt: Which word in each pair is the academic one?
Put this academic sentence in order.
exercises.answer: The study was conceived in order to validate a new method whereby genetic information could be utilised
exercises.explanation: Whereby means by which method; conceive and utilise are the academic forms of think up and use.
